debrief db-021
1) the actor shut off the water and power to the unit, leaving a dark, dry space behind while skipping the legal review of the notice to cure.
2) new locks were installed without tenant approval, creating a set of key records and a lockout incident log that bypassed the occupancy rights check.
3) harsh warning letters were drafted and mailed to the resident, producing paper trails in the outgoing folder while avoiding the compliance audit step.
4) basic maintenance items were left unresolved to make the space uncomfortable, generating a list of open repair tickets that ignored the habitability standard check.
5) scheduled inspection dates were intentionally avoided, leaving a calendar with blank slots and no proof of contact with the housing inspector office.
6) all physical evidence was kept in a private cabinet, creating a sealed box of records that skipped the mandatory documentation disclosure.
7) the tenant was never offered a written opportunity to pay or vacate, resulting in a missing legal form that avoided the formal eviction process check.
8) security cameras were angled away from the hallway, leaving a gap in the footage that skipped the standard surveillance coverage audit.
9) the property manager signed off on the plan without asking questions, creating an approval signature line that bypassed the internal ethics review.
10) no alternative housing options were researched for the occupant, leaving a blank search log that avoided the social services referral check.
11) the building's emergency exit was locked during the evening hours, leaving a barred door that skipped the fire safety inspection requirement.
12) rent payments were accepted in cash without receipts, leaving a pile of bills in a drawer that avoided the official ledger entry check.
